correctness.rationale: For omitted vertices on the same bipartition side, equal locating traces occur exactly when two distinct matched indices are doubly omitted, giving the sharp condition \(|I\cap J|\le1\). Domination contributes only the empty-side and singleton-selected-side obstructions stated in the theorem. These disjoint cases give the bivariate polynomial. The lower bound \(|S|\ge n-1\) follows from \(|I|+|J|\le n+1\); equality configurations are counted exactly. The standalone checker exhaustively verifies the definition, classification, coefficients, minima and totals for \(5\le n\le7\).

value.rationale: Crown graphs are a canonical twin-free bipartite family lying one vertex below the half-order locating-domination barrier for \(n\ge5\). The theorem upgrades a broad existence bound to a complete structural description, a two-variable enumerator, a minimum-set count, and the total count. The matching-index criterion is reusable for separation-code questions on matching-deleted bipartite graphs, so the result is more than a routine scalar computation.
